concept: A banner is a line written on the pane. One sheet of glass stays one layer, and only a small glyph carries the tone colour.

default_to_avoid.pattern: start-edge accent stripe, tinted icon disc, bold title over muted body, a box inside the pane (Carbon inline notification, Material banner, every admin template)
default_to_avoid.why_not: it treats a floating pane as a page and the message as a form error, adds a second surface inside one sheet of glass, and paints the tone in colour the scene should own

derivation.consequence: a soft shadow below and a rim of light on the top-left edge say where the pane floats
derivation.form: a message that needs attention is its own object with its own shadow and rim, placed relative to the pane it is about

derivation.consequence: panes enter by rising a short distance and settling, as an object placed in space would
derivation.form: the message arrives by rising a few pixels and settling instead of fading in place

derivation.consequence: the scene supplies the hue; the system owns almost no colour of its own
derivation.form: no tinted fill or stripe; the tone colour appears only on a small glyph

derivation.consequence: status is spoken in text as well as shown in colour
derivation.form: each tone has its own glyph shape and the tone is spoken as a word before the message

derivation.consequence: the loud action sits apart from secondary ones, never between them
derivation.form: a message action sits at the far end of the message, never inline with the pane own actions

derivation.consequence: movement distances are small (a 2px lift, an 8 to 16px rise) so the layout never appears to move
derivation.form: a banner that arrives or leaves opens and closes its own height smoothly, so the content below slides instead of jumping

variants.note: 2026-10-27: user picked C and asked for the whole family (tones, detail, action, dismiss, stacking, motion, overflow, page surfaces)

root.why: the banner has no surface of its own, because a second fill inside one sheet of glass would be a second layer that is not there

leaving.why: a dismissed banner closes its own height before it is removed, so the content below slides up instead of jumping

line.why: the line clips its content while its row opens or closes, so the pane grows smoothly and nothing overlaps

glyph.why: each tone has its own glyph shape (circle, check, triangle, octagon), and the shape alone tells the tones apart for anyone who cannot see the colour

info.why: information marks its glyph in the bright accent and leaves the rest of the line to the scene

positive.why: success marks only its glyph in green; the pane keeps the colour of its scene

warning.why: warnings mark only the glyph in amber, darker in the light theme so the glyph stays visible on lifted glass

critical.why: errors mark only the glyph in red, never a fill, so an error does not repaint the pane

text.why: title and detail form one reading block that wraps before the actions, read top to bottom

title.why: the title is the only semibold text in the line, which makes the message the first thing the eye catches with no coloured box around it

detail.why: detail uses the measured secondary text colour so it reads as subordinate to the title

sr.why: a hidden word (Warning, Error…) is spoken before the title, because neither the glyph colour nor its shape is read aloud

end.why: actions and dismiss sit apart at the end of the line, never between the words, and wrap below on narrow panes

dismiss.why: dismiss is a quiet 32px disc with a 44px press area, named after what it does

hover.why: hovering dismiss gives it a quiet disc and the primary text colour, answering the pointer without moving anything

focus-visible.why: keyboard focus on dismiss draws the shared ring with its halo, visible on any scene

@media forced-colors: active.why: forced colours draw the hairline and the glyph in the system text colour so the line and its tone shape stay visible

color.why: the dismiss icon colour eases at hover pace with its disc so both read as one response

background-color.why: the dismiss disc fades in at hover pace instead of switching on

@banner-open.why: a new banner opens its row from zero height over the enter duration, so content below is pushed gently rather than jumping

@banner-close.why: closing reverses the opening at the shorter hover pace, because leaving is a reply to the dismiss press
